mainTopic: Making an עירוב with a גוי through his שכיר or לקיט; respect for Torah teachings; wine, הוראה and תפילה; keeping a גר's property
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a discussion about a מבוי shared by Jews and a גוי. רבא knocks down a suggestion to let the Jews carry without an עירוב, and then each fix offered for it: a reminder עירוב, and a public announcement. His solution is that one Jew borrows a spot in the גוי's property and so becomes like the גוי's שכיר or לקיט. Following שמואל's ruling, such a worker may give the עירוב in the גוי's place, and רב יוסף adds that this leniency never becomes a stringency. רב נחמן praises that ruling of שמואל but calls a different one, about not ruling after a רביעית of wine, 'not excellent'. רבא rebukes him for grading Torah teachings, and רב נחמן takes it back. רבה בר רב הונא then rules on praying after drinking: a שתוי's prayer still counts after the fact, but a שיכור's prayer is תועבה. A story of two scholars parting at a river gives the test: whether he could speak before a king. It also gives a second teaching, that one who takes a גר's property should buy a ספר תורה with it. רב ששת's addition to that teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: This would erase the idea of an עירוב from that alley
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects to the earlier suggestion, because the Jews in this מבוי would end up carrying with no עירוב at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, you have wiped out the law of עירוב from that alleyway!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the earlier suggestion. Under it, the Jews in this מבוי carry freely without any עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Technically the alley counts as if only one person lives there, so no עירוב is needed. The problem is what people see: residents carrying with no עירוב. Onlookers will conclude that alleys never need an עירוב, and the whole practice of עירוב will be forgotten there.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces the bad result of the other side's view
The law or practice of עירוב
An alleyway that courtyards open into

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the carrying is actually forbidden by the strict law. His worry is that people will learn the wrong lesson and forget about עירוב.

phrases.english: If so, you have abolished
the law of eruv from that alleyway!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion from the previous section of the daf, which allowed carrying in this alley without an עירוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier suggestion that the alley's residents may carry without an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if this is technically allowed, it looks like carrying without an עירוב. That will make the practice of עירוב disappear from this alley.

steps.title: They make an עירוב anyway as a reminder
steps.stepSummary: The defender answers that the residents still make an עירוב, purely as a reminder.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The defending side answers רבא in a single word. The residents should make an עירוב anyway, even though they don't legally need it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This עירוב has no legal job here. Its only purpose is to keep the practice alive in people's minds. That directly fixes רבא's worry that the practice would be forgotten.

phrases.english: They make an eruv (as a reminder).
phrases.notes: A one-word answer: the residents make a symbolic עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical fix: a symbolic עירוב is added
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought that carrying without an עירוב would make people forget the practice of עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: A reminder עירוב is made, so the practice is not forgotten.

steps.title: People will think an עירוב works even where a גוי lives
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that the reminder עירוב creates a new mistake: people will think an עירוב works even when the גוי has not rented out his space.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then people will say that an עירוב works even in a place where a גוי lives!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back against the fix from step 2. He points out that it creates a different problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real הלכה is that an עירוב does not help when a גוי lives in the alley, unless his space is rented. Onlookers who see an עירוב followed by carrying will think the עירוב is what allowed it. They will then wrongly believe that an עירוב works even with a גוי present.

keyTerms.meaning: People will say: introduces a worry about public misunderstanding
In a place where a גוי lives

phrases.english: They will say an eruv is effective
in the place of a gentile?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fix of making a reminder עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reminder עירוב gives the false impression that an עירוב works even when a גוי's space has not been rented.

steps.title: We announce that the עירוב is only a reminder
steps.stepSummary: The defender answers that we make a public announcement explaining why the residents may really carry.
steps.simpleTranslation: We make an announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The defending side answers רבא again: we announce publicly that the עירוב is only a reminder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The announcement explains that the residents are not carrying because of the עירוב. That should stop people from concluding that an עירוב works where a גוי lives.

keyTerms.meaning: That we make a public announcement

phrases.english: We make an announcement.
phrases.notes: The announcement makes clear that the עירוב is not what allows the carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought people would misread the reminder עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: An announcement explains the situation, so nobody misreads it.

steps.title: Children won't understand an announcement
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the announcement fix. Children who see the עירוב will not hear or understand the announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we make an announcement for the little children?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the announcement idea. The children watching will not get the message.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adults may hear the announcement, but small children only remember what they saw. When they grow up, they will recall that their fathers made an עירוב here. They will then think an עירוב works even where a גוי lives, so the defender's whole approach fails.
steps.whatToRemember: Every fix that keeps the original approach still teaches someone the wrong lesson. That is why the גמרא needs a completely new solution.

phrases.english: An announcement for the children?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The announcement fix, and with it the whole approach of carrying without a real rental from the גוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Children never hear or understand the announcement. They will grow up with a mistaken idea of the הלכה.

steps.title: רבא's solution: become like the gentile's worker
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests that one Jew make friends with the גוי, borrow a spot in his property, and leave an item there. This makes him like the גוי's שכיר or לקיט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: let one of them go and get close to the גוי. He should ask him for a spot and put some item down there. This makes him like the גוי's hired worker or harvester.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the earlier approach failed, רבא offers a new solution that works through the gentile's property itself. A Jew gets permission to use part of the גוי's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By leaving an item in the גוי's space, the Jew gains a foothold there, like a hired worker who uses his employer's property. This sets up the next step, which explains why being like a worker matters: such a worker can act for the גוי in the עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the previous approach and offers a new one
Let him get close to him; make friends with him

steps.whyThisMatters: This solution needs no symbolic עירוב and no announcement. It works through a real legal mechanism, so nobody is misled.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Let one of them go and become friendly with him,
and ask him for a place
and set something down in it,
so that he becomes like his hired laborer or harvester,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected approach of steps 1 through 5 with a new solution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A Jew borrows space from the גוי and becomes like his שכיר or לקיט. That allows a valid עירוב.

steps.title: שמואל: a hired worker can contribute the עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רבא's solution is backed by שמואל's ruling, quoted by רב יהודה: even the גוי's שכיר or לקיט may give the עירוב on the גוי's behalf, and that is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: even his hired worker, and even his harvester, may give his עירוב, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from שמואל to show why רבא's solution works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל rules that a שכיר or לקיט who uses the גוי's property may handle the עירוב for that property. Once the Jew has become like the גוי's worker, he can act for the גוי's space. That makes the עירוב of the whole alley valid.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is enough for him

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer: one Jew borrows a spot from the גוי, becomes like his שכיר or לקיט, and through שמואל's rule can contribute the עירוב on the גוי's behalf.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Even his hired laborer and even his harvester
may contribute his eruv, and that is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the legal basis for רבא's solution in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that becoming like the גוי's worker allows a valid עירוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling, quoted by רב יהודה, that a שכיר or לקיט may contribute the עירוב.

steps.title: What if there are five workers?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף what the law is when the גוי has several Jewish hired workers or harvesters, not just one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: If there were five hired workers and five harvesters there, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a follow-up question about the rule we just learned: what happens when the גוי has many workers instead of one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned that one שכיר or לקיט can stand in for the גוי and help the courtyard. אביי asks whether having many of them makes things harder. For example, would every one of them now have to be part of the עירוב?

keyTerms.meaning: His hired worker (the גוי's paid laborer)
His harvester (a worker who gathers crops for the גוי)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
If there were five of his hired workers there
and five of his harvesters, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He's asking whether having lots of workers makes things stricter.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ שָׁם חֲמִשָּׁה שְׂכִירוֹ וַחֲמִשָּׁה לְקִיטוֹ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far שמואל's שכיר/לקיט rule from Step 7 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does having many שכירים or לקיטים create a stringency, such as requiring all of them to join the עירוב?

steps.title: A leniency does not become a stringency
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the שכיר/לקיט rule was given only to make things easier. It cannot be turned into a reason to make things harder.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: If the חכמים said that his hired worker and harvester count in order to be lenient, would they say his hired worker and harvester count in order to be strict?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי: the many workers do not make anything harder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason the workers count at all is to give the residents an easy way out. A rule created to help cannot be used to add new burdens. So having five workers changes nothing, and one of them is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: To be lenient, to make things easier
To be strict, to make things harder

steps.whatToRemember: The שכיר/לקיט rule is only a קולא (leniency). It is never used to create a חומרא (stringency).

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם אָמְרוּ שְׂכִירוֹ וּלְקִיטוֹ לְהָקֵל,
phrases.english: He said to him: If they said his hired worker and harvester count in order to be lenient,
would they say his hired worker and harvester count in order to be strict?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question. The answer is obviously no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמְרוּ שְׂכִירוֹ וּלְקִיטוֹ לְהָקֵל יֹאמְרוּ שְׂכִירוֹ וּלְקִיטוֹ לְהַחֲמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The workers count only as a leniency. Having many of them adds no stringency.

steps.title: Back to שמואל's ruling, which רב נחמן praises
steps.stepSummary: Using the word גופא, the גמרא returns to שמואל's ruling that a שכיר or לקיט may give the עירוב. רב נחמן calls it an excellent teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Even his hired worker, and even his harvester, may give his עירוב, and that is enough. רב נחמן said: How excellent this teaching is!
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to look at שמואל's ruling on its own. This sets up a new discussion about how רב נחמן reacted to שמואל's rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is the same one quoted in Step 7. Here it is repeated for a new reason: to record רב נחמן's praise. That praise prepares the contrast in the next steps, where he criticizes a different ruling of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself.' The גמרא returns to examine a statement quoted earlier.
Gives his share of the עירוב

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. It is the same ruling of שמואל from Step 7. The גמרא repeats it with גופא so it can add רב נחמן's comment.

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Even his hired worker, and even his harvester,
may give his eiruv, and that is enough.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: כַּמָּה מְעַלְּיָא הָא שְׁמַעְתָּא.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: How excellent is this teaching!

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the source from Step 7 in order to record רב נחמן's praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גוי's שכיר or לקיט may give the עירוב in the גוי's place, and that is enough. רב נחמן praises this ruling.

steps.title: שמואל: someone who drank wine should not rule
steps.stepSummary: A second ruling of שמואל, also quoted by רב יהודה: a person who drank a רביעית of wine should not give rulings of הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If someone drank a רביעית of wine, he should not give a ruling of הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of שמואל. This sets up a ruling that רב נחמן did not like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine can cloud a person's thinking. So שמואל says a person should not decide הלכה after drinking a רביעית. The ruling is quoted here because of how רב נחמן reacts to it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a לוג, the standard measure of wine that can affect the mind
He should not give a halachic ruling

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If one drank a quarter-log of wine, he may not issue a ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: שָׁתָה רְבִיעִית יַיִן אַל יוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of שמואל, brought to contrast with the one רב נחמן praised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who drank a רביעית of wine should not give rulings of הלכה.

steps.title: רב נחמן: this ruling is not excellent
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן criticizes שמואל's wine ruling based on his own experience. Without a רביעית of wine, his mind is not clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: This teaching is not excellent, because as for me, as long as I have not drunk a רביעית of wine, my mind is not clear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן pushes back against שמואל's wine ruling and calls it 'not excellent.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: His argument comes from his own life: wine actually helps him think clearly. So for him, a רביעית does not stop him from ruling. This is the opposite of the praise he gave in Step 10.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לָא מְעַלְּיָא הָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: This teaching is not excellent,
for as for me, as long as
I have not drunk a quarter-log of wine,
my mind is not clear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ruling quoted in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: שמואל's ruling that a person who drank a רביעית should not rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For רב נחמן personally, wine clears his mind instead of clouding it.

steps.title: רבא: do not rank Torah teachings
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן for calling one teaching nice and another not nice. He quotes רבי אחא בר חנינא, who reads משלי as saying that such a person loses the wealth of Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Why did the master say this? Didn't רבי אחא בר חנינא say: What does the verse mean, 'One who keeps company with זונות loses wealth'? Anyone who says 'This teaching is nice (זו נאה) and this one is not nice' loses the wealth of Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא objects to the way רב נחמן spoke, saying 'excellent' about one teaching and 'not excellent' about another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is not arguing about wine or about עירוב. He is challenging the attitude of grading Torah teachings. He uses a wordplay: זונות sounds like 'זו נאה' ('this one is nice'), so a person who picks favorites among teachings 'loses his wealth' of Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?
'This one is nice.' A wordplay on זוֹנוֹת.

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches respect for every Torah teaching. A person may disagree with a ruling, but should not dismiss it as 'not nice.'

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
What is the reason the Master said this?
Didn't Rabbi Acha bar Chanina say:
What is meant by what is written: 'He who keeps company with prostitutes wastes wealth'?
Anyone who says: This teaching is nice,
and this one is not nice,
loses the wealth of Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רב נחמן spoke in Steps 10 and 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's praising one teaching and criticizing another
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Based on רבי אחא בר חנינא's reading of משלי, ranking Torah teachings as nice or not nice makes a person lose the wealth of Torah.

steps.title: רב נחמן takes it back
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן accepts רבא's rebuke and says: I retract.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן agrees with רבא and takes back what he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן does not defend himself. He openly admits his mistake, which shows how seriously the חכמים treated respect for Torah. This closes the discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: I retract, I take it back

steps.whatToRemember: Even a great חכם like רב נחמן withdrew his words. One should not call one Torah teaching 'nice' and another 'not nice.'

phrases.english: He said to him: I retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבא's challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן retracts. One should not grade Torah teachings as nice or not nice.

steps.title: Praying after drinking wine: two levels
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that a שתוי and a שיכור both should not pray. After the fact, a שתוי's prayer counts, but a שיכור's prayer is an abomination.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: someone who has drunk should not pray, but if he did pray, his prayer is a valid prayer. Someone who is drunk should not pray, and if he did pray, his prayer is an abomination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stays on the subject of wine and brings a new ruling about praying after drinking. It sets up two levels of drinking with two different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up front, neither person should pray. The difference appears only after the fact. A שתוי has still fulfilled his obligation, but a שיכור's prayer is worse than nothing; it is called תועבה.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has drunk some wine but is not fully drunk
His prayer is a valid prayer

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a שתוי is allowed to pray. Neither one should pray at the start. The two differ only in what happens if they already prayed.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
One who has drunk should not pray,
but if he prayed, his prayer is a prayer.
phrases.notes: He has fulfilled his obligation after the fact.

phrases.english: One who is drunk should not pray,
and if he prayed, his prayer is an abomination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from wine and הוראה (steps 11-14) to wine and תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither a שתוי nor a שיכור should pray. After the fact, a שתוי's prayer counts, but a שיכור's prayer is תועבה.

steps.title: What counts as having drunk, and what counts as drunk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the definitions of שתוי and שיכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a שתוי, and what is the case of a שיכור?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the line is between the two levels of drinking. This sets up the answer, which comes through a story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in step 15 gives very different results for the two levels, so we need a clear test to tell them apart. The question asks for that test.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of one who has drunk,
and what are the circumstances of one who is drunk?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי שָׁתוּי, וְהֵיכִי דָּמֵי שִׁיכּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definitions of the two terms used in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical line between שתוי and שיכור.

steps.title: Two scholars part ways with words of Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells a story about רבי אבא בר שומני and רב מנשיא בר ירמיה, who were parting at a river. They agreed that each would say something new, following מרי בר רב הונא's teaching that one should part from a friend with a matter of הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what happened when רבי אבא בר שומני and רב מנשיא בר ירמיה from Gifti were parting from each other at the crossing of the Yofti river. They said: let each of us say something the other has not heard. For מרי בר רב הונא said: a person should part from his friend only with a matter of הלכה, because that way he will remember him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the answer to its question by telling a story. The actual definition comes in the next step, from one of the two scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story also teaches its own lesson along the way. When parting from a friend, share a הלכה, because it makes the friend remember you.

keyTerms.meaning: His friend has not heard it

steps.whyThisMatters: מרי בר רב הונא's rule, to part from a friend with a דבר הלכה, is a well-known practice in its own right.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר שׁוּמְנִי
phrases.english: As in this case, when Rabbi Abba bar Shumni
and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeya from Gifti
were taking leave of each other
at the crossing of the Yofti river.
They said: let each one of us
say something that his friend has not heard,
for Mari bar Rav Huna said:
A person should not part from his friend
except with a matter of halacha,
because through this he remembers him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר שׁוּמְנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 16 by introducing the story in which the definition was taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should part from his friend with a matter of הלכה, so the friend will remember him.

steps.title: The test: can he speak before a king?
steps.stepSummary: One scholar defines the terms. A שתוי can still speak properly before a king. A שיכור cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of them opened and said: what is a שתוי and what is a שיכור? A שתוי is anyone who is able to speak before a king. A שיכור is anyone who is not able to speak before a king.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the גמרא's question from step 16 gets its answer. The first scholar gives the test that separates the two levels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line is not set by how much wine he drank. It is set by his condition: is he clear enough to stand and speak properly before a king? This fits תפילה well, since prayer is standing before the King of kings.
steps.whatToRemember: שתוי means he can still speak before a king, so his prayer counts after the fact. שיכור means he cannot, so his prayer is תועבה.

phrases.english: One opened and said:

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי שָׁתוּי, וְהֵיכִי דָּמֵי שִׁיכּוֹר?
phrases.english: What is the case of one who has drunk, and what is the case of one who is drunk?
phrases.notes: The scholar opens his teaching by asking the question again.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁתוּי — כֹּל שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְדַבֵּר לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ.
phrases.english: One who has drunk is anyone who is able to speak before the king.
One who is drunk is anyone who is not able
to speak before the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the first scholar's teaching, which answers step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שתוי means he can speak before a king. שיכור means he cannot.

steps.title: Keeping a convert's property: buy a Torah scroll
steps.stepSummary: The second scholar teaches that a person who took possession of a גר's property should buy a ספר תורה with it, so that the property will stay with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other one opened and said: someone who takes hold of the property of a גר, what should he do so that it lasts in his hands? He should buy a ספר תורה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the second scholar shares his new teaching, which is on a completely different topic. It is the second half of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר who dies without heirs leaves property that has no owner, and whoever grabs it first acquires it. Since this gain did not come from the person's own work, it may not last. Using part of it for a מצוה like a ספר תורה earns the merit for him to keep the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: The property of a convert (who died without heirs)
And they will last in his hands

steps.confusionAlert: This teaching has nothing to do with wine or prayer. It is simply the second scholar's "new thing" from the story.

phrases.english: The other one opened and said:
One who takes possession of a convert's property,
what should he do so that it remains in his hands?
He should buy a Torah scroll with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the story with the second scholar's teaching, which opens a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who took a גר's property should buy a ספר תורה with it so the property will stay with him.

steps.title: רב ששת begins to add to the teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת starts a statement with the word "even", adding to the teaching about the גר's property. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Even...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new statement from רב ששת. It will expand the ספר תורה teaching, but the rest of his words are on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אפילו shows that רב ששת is about to stretch the teaching to include a wider case. We will see what he adds when the text continues.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: Even
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an expansion of the teaching about the גר's property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incomplete on this amud. רב ששת's expansion begins with "even" and continues on the next amud.
